title: Quality Inspector (NDT/QMS)
description: Overview & Responsibilities We are seeking a highly meticulous Quality Inspector to join our Supply Chain department. In this critical operational role, you will be the frontline safeguard for the Ebara Elliott Energy's Quality Management System, ensuring the absolute integrity of precision turbomachinery parts and components. Your primary focus will involve rigorous quality checks on critical materials destined for steam turbines, centrifugal compressors, and both multistage and cryogenic pumps. By verifying that all incoming materials, in-process assemblies, and final products meet our stringent engineering standards, you will directly support our commitment to delivering world-class, reliable turbomachinery equipment. Job Responsibilities Interpret Technical Documentation: Read, analyze, and accurately apply complex engineering documentation, including work orders, assembly and manufacturing blueprints, special instructions, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and material specifications specific to turbomachinery. Execute Precision Measurements: Utilize a comprehensive array of manual and digital measuring devices to perform dimensional inspections, ensuring that turbine, compressor, and pump components strictly conform to drawing tolerances, quality standards, and completeness requirements. Conduct NDT Inspections: Perform thorough incoming, in-process, and final Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) inspections across various stages of the supply chain lifecycle to identify surface and subsurface defects. Manage Quality Documentation: Initiate and process critical quality control documentation, including scrap and rework reports, Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs), and comprehensive quality action reports to track and resolve discrepancies. Maintain Equipment Calibration: Oversee the calibration processes and maintain meticulous logs for all inspection and measuring equipment, encompassing both company-issued quality center tools and personally owned precision instruments. Verify Incoming Supply Chain Materials: Inspect, identify, and formally approve incoming raw materials and outsourced components, verifying they match engineering drawings and material specifications before being released to the floor. Execute Operational Priorities: Effectively manage daily workflow by receiving, prioritizing, and adhering to inspection schedules and urgent operational targets set by supply chain management. Escalate Non-Conformances: Proactively identify, thoroughly document, and raise immediate awareness regarding any material or procedural non-conformances to the appropriate engineering and management teams. Uphold Safety and 5S Standards: Strictly adhere to all facility safety protocols and maintain workstations in a clean, organized, and highly functional operating condition. Author Inspection Reports: Draft clear, concise, and highly accurate inspection reports to maintain a permanent, traceable record for all evaluated parts. Validate Supplier Compliance: Review and analyze Material Test Reports (MTRs) provided by external suppliers to guarantee absolute compliance with Elliott's proprietary material specifications. Perform Final Release Inspections: Conduct rigorous final quality inspections on all finished turbomachinery parts and components prior to their approval for shipment or inventory storage. Required Qualifications & Skills: Experience: A minimum of two (2) years of dedicated inspection and quality control experience within an industrial, manufacturing, or supply chain environment. Rotating Equipment & Turbomachinery experience with an OEM is highly preferred. NDT Knowledge: Strong foundational understanding of core Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) methodologies, specifically Penetrant Testing (PT), Ultrasonic Testing (UT), Radiographic Testing (RT), and Magnetic Particle Testing (MT). Advanced Certifications (Preferred): Highly qualified candidates will possess an active ASNT Level 2 certification in Visual Testing (VT) or possess the prerequisite training to obtain it. Equipment Proficiency: Demonstrated hands-on experience utilizing a broad spectrum of specialized NDT equipment and advanced precision measuring tools. Dimensional Tool Mastery: High proficiency in reading and operating manual and digital measuring tools, including micrometers, calipers, dial indicators, height gauges, and related inspection instruments. NDT Hardware Operation: Practical familiarity with operating non-destructive testing hardware, such as magnetic particle yokes/machines, ultrasonic flaw detectors, digital thickness indicators, and ultraviolet (black light) equipment. Technical Comprehension: Exceptional ability to accurately read and interpret complex mechanical scopes of work, detailed blueprints, special engineering procedures, and technical component specifications. Operational Flexibility: Willingness to work overtime and alternating shifts as required to support fluctuating plant operations, production schedules, and supply chain demands. Education: A high school diploma or equivalent is required; candidates with advanced or specialized technical training in quality control, metallurgy, or machining will be given strong preference. Software Skills: Familiarity with the Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook) for report generation, data entry, and internal communication. Customers throughout the world choose Elliott for the design, manufacture and service of their critical rotating equipment. Elliott’s global service network routinely installs, overhauls, repairs, upgrades and rerates machines from any manufacturer. This role does not require coding ability, but candidates with hands-on technical fluency (SQL, scripting, API / data literacy) will be considered a strong asset given the complexity of the systems involved. What We’re Looking For Four qualities define success in this role: A Self-Starter and Owner — You take end-to-end ownership of your platform’s SDLC without waiting to be directed. Technically Fluent — You are comfortable in the details of a complex payments platform — transaction flows, data models, integrations, and configuration — and can hold a credible technical conversation with engineers and QA. You reason about systems, not just features. Rigorous and Complete — You do not stop at the happy path. Before a change is committed, you systematically map its full impact surface — every transaction type, user persona, device population, credential form, processing feature, integration rail, and configuration state it could touch — so nothing is silently left behind. Completeness of analysis is the single most important thing this role protects. Strong analytical and process-design skills, with comfort interpreting data to monitor transactional and non-transactional activity. High proficiency in written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate effectively with a US-based team and accurately translate their business requirements into clear PRDs and project plans. Demonstrated comfort using AI tools (e.g., for documentation, analysis, or workflow automation) as part of regular product management practice. A collaborative work style and willingness to work a hybrid schedule from Valor PayTech’s Chennai office. Experience reporting to or partnering closely with a Product Owner in a structured product organization. Nice to Have (Strong Bonus) US Payment Knowledge, credit card processing and working on ISV products POS machines development, APP building, API integration Web Apps development and payment integration Familiarity with payments infrastructure and terminology — processors (such as TSYS, Fiserv), ACH / NACHA, ISO 8583, PCI DSS — gained through hands-on product or technical work. Big plus – but not required. Working knowledge of SQL for querying transaction, settlement, or merchant data. Scripting ability (e.g., Python) to support data analysis, automation, or reporting tasks. Exposure to REST APIs, JSON / XML data structures, or systems integration concepts. Prior experience with risk / fraud monitoring tools or chargeback and dispute workflows. Certifications such as CSPO, PMI-ACP, or processor-specific training (e.g., TSYS University). Why Join Valor PayTech You’ll take ownership of a mission-critical platform that touches every stage of the Valor payment gateway and ISV relationship, working alongside a focused product and engineering team in our Chennai office. This is an opportunity to shape how a fast-growing Payment gateway integrating with ISVs to utilize our feature — and to set the standard for how analysis and requirements are done — with direct visibility into the Product and broader leadership team.

description: QA Engineer Key Responsibilities Own whether the platform is safe to release — the automated suite, the manual passes automation cannot replace, and the judgement about what a failing test actually means Build and keep the end-to-end suite in Playwright across the journeys that matter — a patient booked, registered, seen, billed, dispensed to and reported on — and keep it fast and trustworthy enough that nobody is tempted to ignore a red build Write the test plan for each module from what the hospital does rather than from what the screen shows, with the Business Analyst and the module owner in the room Own the regression pack that runs before every release, and grow it every time something escapes Run beta: put each release in front of the hospital's own people on migrated data, log what they find so it can be reproduced, and close it before the next release starts Be the person who says a release is not ready, and be right often enough that it carries weight Where Testing Is Mandatory Money — every path that produces a bill, a discount, a refund or a day-end total, including the ones that fail halfway through Stock — batch, expiry, issue and return, and the concurrent case where two counters sell the last strip Clinical safety — allergy and interaction checks, dose limits by age and weight, critical values, and every alert that must reach a human Access — that one hospital cannot see another's data, and that a role cannot do what it should not Integrations — a laboratory result from a real analyser, an image from a real modality, an ABHA created against the real sandbox; a mock proves the code, not the hospital Test the failure paths as seriously as the happy ones; the happy path is the one everybody already tried Beta, Parallel Run and Go-Live Turn the acceptance scripts into something the hospital's own staff can run and sign, on their own migrated data, in the beta environment Design the parallel run: what is entered in both systems, what is reconciled daily, and what "the numbers match" means for registrations, bills, collections, dispensing and reports Be on the floor through cutover and hypercare, where the real testing happens, and bring what you see back into the suite Own test data: realistic, safe, and reproducible, including the awkward records that break things — the duplicate patient, the expired batch, the refund after a partial payment Working With the Team Sit in on specification work early, because the cheapest defect is the one caught while the specification is still a paragraph Keep every defect described so that someone who was not there can reproduce it — steps, data, environment, what was expected, what happened Track what escaped and why, and bring it to the retrospective rather than to an individual Pair with engineers on the automated checks that live beside the code, so testing is not a gate at the end but a habit along the way Tech Stack Playwright · TypeScript · pytest · Python · FastAPI · PostgreSQL · SQL · REST · OpenAPI · GitHub Actions · Docker · HL7 v2 · FHIR · ABDM We build in Python on FastAPI with React in front of it, on Amazon Web Services, and we test it with Playwright and pytest. That is what this role writes, runs and reads every day, and we would rather say it plainly at the top than have you find out in week one. What you will work in every day End-to-end testing — Playwright with TypeScript, against the real web application: journeys, fixtures, test data builders, and traces that say why a run failed API and service testing — pytest and pytest-asyncio against FastAPI services; the OpenAPI schema is the contract, and tests are written to it Database verification — PostgreSQL and SQL good enough to prove in the database what the screen claims, and to spot the migration that silently rounded a rupee Continuous integration — GitHub Actions; the suite runs on every pull request, and a red build blocks a merge Environments — Docker-based environments for development, beta and UAT, each with its own reproducible data set Performance — load testing at peak outpatient volume with k6 or Locust, and the judgement to know which number matters Integration test beds — HL7 v2 messages from analysers over MLLP, DICOM modality worklist and PACS, and the ABDM sandbox for ABHA creation and consent Defect and test management — a shared tracker visible to the hospital, with a published severity and response standard What we need you to have used in production Playwright, Cypress or Selenium on a system people depended on — writing maintainable tests, not recording brittle ones A programming language , enough to write helpers, fixtures and data builders; (TASE) Industry: Aerospace and Precision Engineering / Manufacturing Department: Quality Assurance Reports To: Quality Engineer / Quality Manager Job Purpose To verify that finished components, assemblies, and products conform to approved customer drawings, specifications, regulatory requirements, and company quality standards before final acceptance and release. Key Responsibilities Perform final inspections and First Article Inspection (FAI), as assigned, on parts, materials, components, sub-assemblies, assemblies, tooling, and final product configurations against customer blueprints, sketches, engineering drawings, purchase orders, and other applicable requirements. Review relevant contracts, purchase orders, drawings, routings, shop instructions, inspection plans, and associated records to verify applicable quality and acceptance requirements. Support the qualification of new products and verify that applicable production and engineering qualification processes comply with approved methods and procedures. Ensure appropriate inspection methods, calibrated measuring instruments, tools, sampling plans, and acceptance criteria are applied in accordance with customer and company requirements. Verify critical dimensions, characteristics, product identification, marking, traceability, and applicable documentation before final acceptance. Exercise sound judgment in assessing critical components and identifying deviations that may affect product conformity, functionality, safety, or customer requirements. Record variable inspection data and measurement results in Detailed Inspection Plans (DIP), final inspection reports, and other approved quality records. Identify, segregate, document, and report nonconforming materials or finished products in accordance with established non-conformance procedures. Conduct receiving inspections when assigned, ensuring incoming materials and components meet applicable purchase, drawing, and specification requirements. Support Production and Quality teams in continuous improvement, root-cause analysis, rejection reduction, and corrective-action activities. Ensure inspection documentation, material traceability, and applicable quality records are complete and accurate before recommending or authorizing product release, as per delegated authority. Communicate inspection findings and quality concerns effectively with Production, Engineering, Quality, suppliers, and customers, as required. Ensure compliance with applicable AS9100, ISO 13485, customer-specific requirements, and approved Quality Management System procedures. Perform other duties consistent with the position, as required or assigned. Qualification & Experience ITI / Diploma in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent qualification. 2–5 years of experience in final inspection within precision machining, aerospace, or engineering manufacturing. Strong knowledge of engineering drawings, GD&T, tolerances, and precision measuring instruments. Familiarity with FAI, inspection documentation, sampling plans, and product traceability is preferred. Key Competencies Dimensional verification, drawing interpretation, inspection judgment, documentation accuracy, non-conformance management, and a strong commitment to product quality.
